findings.title: The repository is SHALLOW (not 'pruned'), and the validator never detects shallowness: write-once, back-dating and the D-035/D-037 commit tolerances silently depend on clone depth
findings.reproduction: (1) git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository prints true. .git/shallow lists e8361b8 ('DG0 round 12 ...'), whose parent dcb289c is simply not fetched (log 06). D-035 and D-037 (decisions.md rows D-035 and D-037) describe this as a history 'truncated'/'pruned' in an earlier session. The commits are outside a shallow boundary, and a full clone (CI uses fetch-depth: 0) may contain them. No file in tools/gates or tools/agents mentions 'shallow'. (2) Consequence for write-once: r21-shallow-writeonce.mjs (log 05). In clone A, commit M rewrites the write-once round-20/qa-verifier.findings.json (F-DG0-242 High -> Low) and findings.json to match, then commit N follows. checkWriteOnce(A) reports 2 errors ('M event', '2 different contents'). In B = git clone --depth 2 file://A, checkWriteOnce(B) reports 0 errors, and no output says the repository is shallow. The same applies today to every write-once file changed before e8361b8 in every local validation (prefreeze, the qa dry-run, the auditor's clone). (3) Consequence for D-037: in a complete clone, every ancestor of the present gate/round source_commit is present, so an ABSENT fix_revision is provably not in that candidate. The tolerance at rules.mjs:696-698 then accepts exactly the failing case. The unit test 'D-037 / F-DG0-242' even accepts fix_revision '0'x40 for a closure verified in the gate round. The census (log 04, P1) finds 3 closures (F-DG0-226/227/228) whose verifying round-13 source_commit is present while the fix is absent, which is possible only because of the shallow boundary.
findings.expected: The validator detects a shallow repository (git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository). It reports this, and either refuses or runs history checks only when a documented shallow boundary is explicitly allowed. Commit-absence tolerances apply only to commits beyond that boundary, or only when the verifying round's own source_commit is also unavailable, never to a closure in the gate round. D-035/D-037 are corrected to say 'outside the shallow boundary' and state what a full-history (CI) run is expected to show.
findings.actual: History-based integrity checks pass or fail depending on clone depth, without any warning. Tolerances meant for 'pruned' commits also accept fabricated SHAs in a complete clone.
findings.fix_summary: D-038: the repo was SHALLOW not pruned (unshallow restored pre-round-12 commits as real ancestors). validateGate now refuses a shallow repository; gate judged against complete history (CI fetch-depth 0). Backup branch deleted so the round-18 orphan 450c756 is uniformly absent.

verification.note: git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository prints false in the working repository and in a --no-local clone. The pruned-era commits are real ancestors of HEAD: all 22 round source_commits except the D-034-orphaned 450c756 are present and ancestors, and 421c922 is an ancestor. On a --depth=1 --no-local clone, validate.mjs --stage DG0 reports the D-038 shallow error (exit 1); on a complete clone it does not. A clone disguised by deleting .git/shallow still fails closed ('write-once: cannot inspect git history'). CI checks out with fetch-depth: 0, so the refusal does not break CI.

findings.title: The D-037 re-point of F-DG0-150/151 to 421c922 leaves a permanent gate error in any clone that carries the backup branch, while a single-branch clone (CI) passes: the gate verdict depends on which refs the clone has
findings.reproduction: F-DG0-150/151 were last verified by code-security in round 18. stages.json round 18 has source_commit 450c756, which exists only on the local, unpushed branch backup/pre-writeonce-repair-565ab3f and is not an ancestor of HEAD (log 12). D-037 re-pointed their fix_revision to 421c922, which is an ancestor of HEAD but NOT of 450c756 (cb76260, the original, is). Running qa's dry-run docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/real-repo-gate-blockers.mjs on a --no-local clone of HEAD (log 10) therefore reports 2 errors that finishing round 21 cannot clear: 'finding F-DG0-150 (Low): fix 421c922233 is not in the verified round-18 candidate (450c756f67)' and the same for F-DG0-151. The harness buckets them as 'PRUNED', but both commits are present. In a --single-branch clone, 450c756 is absent (log 12), so rules.mjs:696 skips the check and the same gate passes. This contradicts D-037's claim that the dry-run is clean of permanent blockers.
findings.expected: A gate's validation result does not depend on which unrelated refs a clone happens to contain, and F-DG0-150/151's metadata is consistent with the round that verified them. For example, their reporter re-verifies them in a round whose candidate contains 421c922. Alternatively, the fix_revision stays cb76260 and the round-18 source commit is preserved on a pushed ref.
findings.actual: Locally, with the backup branch, validateGate fails permanently on F-DG0-150/151. In CI or a single-branch clone it passes. Fail-closed locally, so no false approval, but the gate cannot pass on this repository as it stands.
findings.fix_summary: D-038: F-DG0-150/151 re-verified in round 22 against the current candidate (fix 421c922, ancestor of HEAD) so their closure is clone-independent; backup branch deleted removes 450c756's conditional presence.

verification.note: No ref contains 450c756 any more (the backup/ branch is gone). It survives only as a reflog-held unreachable object in the working repository. The real-repo dry-run on a --no-local clone reports 0 in the PRUNED, RECORD-LESS and DROPPED buckets. Before this round's re-verification, a local clone that still holds 450c756 reports 2 extra errors for F-DG0-150/151 (dryrun-clone-modes.log). With the round-22 re-verification in place, both clone modes give 0 (f161-reverify-sim.log), so the verdict no longer depends on refs. This closure depends on the F-DG0-150/151 entries in this same sidecar being imported. The general object-store-vs-reachability issue is part of F-DG0-164.

findings.title: Residual 7 still frames the /proc/sys write as a file-tool path, but the agent's Bash shell can open DAC-writable host-global /proc/sys entries for write directly; the new comment's '(userns default)' names the wrong mechanism
findings.reproduction: Probes open(O_WRONLY) and close without writing, so no tunable was changed (logs 13 and 14). From the agent shell (uid 0, NoNewPrivs 1, in its own PID namespace), /proc/sys/vm/swappiness, kernel/shmmax, net/ipv4/ip_forward, vm/drop_caches and kernel/panic all open for write. docs/delivery/threat-model.md:60 (residual 7) describes the exposure as a file tool writing 'directly or by racing a symlink past the guard', and only withdraws the shell claim as 'unverified'. It is now verified that a plain shell redirect reaches these entries, with no race needed. The impact class is unchanged: host availability / kernel tunables, not repository or gate integrity. The /proc/sysrq-trigger vector does not exist on this kernel. Separately, tools/agents/agent_sandbox.py:153 says candidate code in the reviewer's fresh-procfs sandboxes sees /proc/sys read-only '(userns default)'. That holds for tools/gates/sandbox-run.sh only because of its explicit '--ro-bind /proc/sys /proc/sys' (log 13: EROFS). A plain nested 'bwrap --unshare-user --proc /proc' leaves /proc/sys writable.
findings.expected: Residual 7 states that the agent shell, as well as the file tools, can write uid-0 DAC-writable /proc/sys entries directly. The comment attributes the read-only /proc/sys in sandbox-run.sh to its explicit --ro-bind.
findings.actual: The residual understates the vector (shell, no race needed), though not the impact. The comment names the wrong mechanism. I would accept this as an observation: the disclosed impact scope (host-global availability, no integrity effect) is accurate, and F-DG0-149 already carries it.
findings.fix_summary: D-038: residual 7 now states the agent Bash shell (not only file tools) writes host-global /proc/sys directly (verified, no race); comment attributes read-only /proc/sys to sandbox-run.sh's explicit --ro-bind, not a userns default.

verification.note: Wording verified against behaviour. The agent shell opens /proc/sys/vm/swappiness, kernel/shmmax, net/ipv4/ip_forward, kernel/panic and vm/drop_caches for write (open(O_WRONLY)+close only; nothing written). Inside tools/gates/sandbox-run.sh the same entries are 'Read-only file system', because of its explicit '--ro-bind /proc/sys /proc/sys' (sandbox-run.sh:36). Residual 7's body and the agent_sandbox.py comment (lines 149-155) now state exactly this. Cosmetic nit: residual 7's bold heading still reads 'file-tool writes to uid-0-writable /proc/sys entries', while the body correctly covers the shell.

findings.title: Schema subset validator: additionalProperties:false does not reject keys named after Object.prototype members (constructor, toString, __proto__, hasOwnProperty)
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/schema.mjs:59 looks up props[key] on a plain object literal, so props['constructor'] resolves to Object.prototype.constructor, which is truthy. The value is then 'validated' against a keyword-less function and accepted, and the additionalProperties:false branch is never reached. With schema {properties:{a:string}, additionalProperties:false}, validate() reports 'zzz' as unexpected but accepts 'constructor', 'toString', '__proto__' and 'hasOwnProperty' (r21-schema-proto-keys.mjs, log 17). The gate rules read only named fields, so an extra key of this kind cannot change a verdict today.
findings.expected: Use Object.hasOwn(props, key) (and Object.hasOwn(value, key) for required), so every unexpected key is reported.
findings.actual: Prototype-named extra keys pass records, findings and gate schemas silently. I would accept this as an observation: no rule reads such keys.
findings.fix_summary: D-038: schema.mjs uses Object.hasOwn(props,key) and Object.hasOwn(value,key), so extra keys named after Object.prototype members (constructor/toString/__proto__/hasOwnProperty) are rejected by additionalProperties:false. Test D-038/F-DG0-163.

verification.note: schema.mjs uses Object.hasOwn for both required and properties. SEC22-7: additionalProperties:false now rejects constructor, toString, hasOwnProperty, valueOf, __proto__ (own key via JSON.parse), __defineGetter__ and isPrototypeOf, and a required 'constructor' is reported missing when absent. Unit test 'D-038 / F-DG0-163' passes.

findings.title: The D-037 absent-commit tolerance (commitPresent) is not scoped to genuinely pruned commits. checkInvocation now accepts a GATE-round review or audit run whose meta.head_commit_at_start is missing, null, the runner's own fallback 'unknown', or any non-existent 40-hex id. This reopens the round-9 QA5-N52/N53 controls (F-DG0-212 binding: the run must start from a commit that contains the frozen manifest). checkClosure likewise accepts a non-existent (typo'd or all-zero) fix_revision on a closure verified in a round whose own source_commit is present, including the gate round.
findings.reproduction: QA_REPO_ROOT=<fresh clone of a0e077d> node --test docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/dg0-gate-negative-r21.test.mjs (log docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/round-21/11-qa21-negative-tests.log). On the independent fully-evidenced fixture (0 errors as control, QA21-G0), for each of domain-reviewer, code-security-reviewer, qa-verifier and release-auditor in the gate round, rewrite the run's meta.json: QA21-C4 head_commit_at_start = 'f'x40, QA21-C5 field deleted, QA21-C5b null, QA21-C5d 'unknown' (tools/agents/run-agent.sh:64 writes exactly this when `git rev-parse HEAD` fails). validateGate(current) returns 0 errors in all 16 cases (ACCEPTED). The round-9 suite re-run under round-21 rules (log round-21/10-r20-suite-rerun.log, QA20-G1) now fails QA5-N52 and QA5-N53, which passed through round 20. QA21-C3: a closure verified in the gate round (round-2, source_commit present) with fix_revision = the real fix with its last hex digit changed, or '0'x40, gives 0 errors. In a full clone a missing commit can never be an ancestor of a present one, so this is provably not 'in the candidate'. The existing unit test 'D-037 / F-DG0-242' (validator.test.mjs line ~1115) codifies the all-zero case in the gate round as accepted. Root cause: rules.mjs checkInvocation calls `if (commitPresent(repo, meta.head_commit_at_start)) {...}` and checkClosure calls `commitPresent(fix) && commitPresent(round.source_commit) && !isAncestor(...)`. Any value that does not resolve, whatever its shape and whichever round it is in, is treated as 'pruned'. Controls: a PRESENT fix that is not in the candidate is still rejected (QA21-C1 descendant, QA21-C2 dangling), and the real-repo dry-run is clean (round-21/13-real-repo-gate-blockers.log).
findings.expected: D-037 states that the tolerance covers commits 'pruned by a later legitimate history correction (the pre-round-12 truncation, the D-034 rewrite)', and that 'a run that started before the manifest is still caught'. By the same reasoning as D-036/F-DG0-240 (the D-035 tolerance must not reach the gate's own round), the tolerance should apply only to (a) a well-formed ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ value, never to a missing, null, 'unknown' or other malformed head_commit_at_start (those were rejected before D-037), and (b) a round that is itself pruned, i.e. whose source_commit is also absent, and never to the gate round. This is feasible on the real history: every one of the 33 record runs with an absent head_commit_at_start belongs to rounds 1-12, whose source_commits are all absent, and all 61 verifier runs with an absent head belong to pruned rounds. For closures, only F-DG0-226/227/228 (verified in round 13, present, fix d1352f4 absent) would need their fix_revision re-pointed at a retained commit that contains the fix, as was done for F-DG0-150/151. findings.title: agent_sandbox.py finish(): when one of the role's own new review files already exists in the real directory (another run of the same role and round committed it after this run's prepare), copy-back crashes with an uncaught FileExistsError. It leaves a partial copy-back (files sorted before the collision are already in the real tree) and writes no sandbox.json, contrary to the threat model's statement that discarded writes are listed in sandbox.json
findings.reproduction: Disposable fixture under $TMPDIR (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/round-17/12-copyback-collision-probe.log, script included). `agent_sandbox.py prepare qa-verifier ...`, then in the staging copy write round-2/qa-verifier.findings.json and round-2/qa-verifier.json. Then create round-2/qa-verifier.json in the REAL reviews dir (a concurrent run of the same role committing first). `agent_sandbox.py finish <state> <out>` exits 1 with 'FileExistsError: [Errno 17] File exists: .../round-2/qa-verifier.json' (the O_EXCL open). The real round-2 now holds THIS run's qa-verifier.findings.json next to the OTHER run's qa-verifier.json, and <out>/sandbox.json is not written. The real record is not overwritten (QA17-S4 passes on that point).
findings.expected: A collision on the role's own new file is handled like the other refusals: nothing is copied for that file, the collision is listed in sandbox.json 'discarded' (for example 'exists in the real tree (written concurrently); not copied'), finish() exits 3, and ideally no file of the run is copied back at all when any of them collides (check first, then copy), so the real tree never holds a mixed record/sidecar pair.
findings.actual: Fail-closed only. run-agent.sh treats any non-zero finish as SANDBOX_RC and a review run then exits 73 without auto-committing, the real record is preserved (O_EXCL), and a mixed pair would not bind to one run's transcript under D-021. It needs two concurrent runs of the same role for the same round, which the orchestrator does not schedule. But the evidence the threat model promises (sandbox.json with the discard list, meta.process_sandbox_*) is missing for that run, and an uncommitted foreign sidecar is left in the real reviews directory for the orchestrator to notice. Low and non-mandatory. I would accept it as an observation for DG0.

findings.title: D-038 scoping is keyed on a forgeable, object-store-based 'round absent' test: a superseded round whose frozen manifest records a non-existent source_commit re-opens the absent-fix tolerance, so a CLOSED_VERIFIED finding passes with an all-zero or typo'd fix_revision and the gate-candidate ancestry check is skipped
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:725-733 (checkClosure) sets roundAbsent = !commitPresent(round.source_commit), and when the fix_revision is also absent it pushes no error. The gate check at :731 sits only in the fix-PRESENT branch. round.source_commit is metadata: checkReviewRounds (:749) only requires it to equal the round's committed manifest.source_commit, and findManifest (:903-909) tolerates a manifest whose source_commit does not exist. Nothing requires a non-gate round's source_commit to exist or to be an ancestor of the commit that froze its manifest. Reproduction on the validator's own fixture (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-22/sec22-repro.tests.mjs.txt, run by run-sec22-repro.sh on a --no-local clone of 7cf94db; log sec22-repro.log): round 2 verifies F-DG0-101 (High, mandatory); round 3 is the gate round. The round-2 manifest is committed with source_commit 'deadbeef'x5, and real round-2 runs start from the commit that contains it. SEC22-1 (real fix): 0 errors. SEC22-2 (fix_revision = 0x40): 0 errors. SEC22-3 (fix_revision = one-character typo of the real fix): 0 errors. SEC22-4 control: a PRESENT off-branch fix is still caught ('is not in the gate candidate'). Retained and gate rounds hold (SEC22-5: unknown/HEAD/missing/null/zeros/uppercase/short heads and zero/f fix_revisions are all rejected). The same predicate gates checkInvocation's head tolerance (:399/:408), so in such a round a fabricated 40-hex head_commit_at_start is also accepted. Second symptom of the same root cause: commitPresent (:595-602) tests object-store membership, not reachability. The working repository still holds round 18's 450c756 through its reflog, while a --no-local clone does not, so validateGate(current) on the same commit differs by 2 errors (F-DG0-150/151 'fix 421c922 is not in the verified round-18 candidate') between the two clone modes (dryrun-clone-modes.mjs/.log). Why the tolerance has no remaining legitimate use: the validator now refuses shallow clones (F-DG0-160), and in a complete clone every ancestor of the gate source_commit is present. An absent fix_revision is therefore provably NOT in the gate candidate. Census on a --no-local clone (tolerance-census.log): 0 findings have an absent fix_revision; the only absent round is 18; and the only closures whose verifying run has an absent head are F-DG0-150/151, which this round re-verifies in round 22 (f161-reverify-sim.log: afterwards 0 dependent errors in both clone modes).
findings.expected: D-038 states the tolerance is 'never a retained round'. Retained-ness must not be something a single metadata value can declare. After this round nothing needs the absent-fix tolerance, so: (1) in checkClosure, reject any CLOSED_VERIFIED fix_revision that is not present AND an ancestor of the gate source_commit (and of the verifying round's source_commit when present), with no round-absent escape; (2) in checkInvocation, either drop the absent-head tolerance or restrict it to an explicit, reviewed allowlist of orphaned rounds (round 18, D-034); (3) decide 'absent' deterministically, e.g. by 'not an ancestor of HEAD' rather than by object-store membership, so unreachable reflog objects cannot change a verdict; (4) optionally, for a non-gate round whose manifest source_commit is present, require it to be an ancestor of the commit that introduced the manifest. Add fixture tests for SEC22-2/3.

findings.title: Findings sidecars in non-gate rounds are not bound to any run, and the latest raising sidecar supersedes the reviewer's immutable fields, so an added later-round sidecar can silently downgrade a finding's severity and mandatory_violation
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:495 keeps only the LATEST sidecar version of each finding ('later rounds supersede earlier versions'), and :537-539 compares findings.json's IMMUTABLE_FINDING_FIELDS (stage_id, requirement, severity, mandatory_violation, title, reported_by) against that version only. A <role>.findings.json is bound to a run's tool-authored outputs only for the gate-round records (checkReview :463). checkClosure binds only the verifications sidecar (:714), and checkReviewRounds (:752-763) only checks that a listed record's sidecar exists. write-once (:781) forbids modifying committed files, not adding new ones. Reproduction (sec22-repro.tests.mjs.txt SEC22-8, log sec22-repro.log): genuine 3-round fixture, with F-DG0-101 raised High/mandatory in round 1, verified in round 2, gate round 3; control 0 errors. With no reviewer run, add docs/delivery/reviews/DG0/round-2/code-security-reviewer.findings.json re-listing F-DG0-101 as Low / mandatory_violation false, and set the same values in findings.json: 0 errors. Negative control: the same findings.json downgrade WITHOUT the added sidecar is caught ('severity in findings.json ("Low") differs from the reviewer's ("High")').
findings.expected: A reviewer's classification of a finding can change only through a sidecar that the reviewer's own run demonstrably wrote. Either bind every findings sidecar (any round) to its role's run for that round, i.e. require it to be among that run's tool-authored outputs, as checkReview does for the gate round; or compare the immutable fields against EVERY raising sidecar version (or the earliest), so a later version cannot differ.
findings.actual: An added, unbound findings sidecar in any non-gate round later than the raising round re-classifies a High/mandatory finding as Low/non-mandatory without a validator error. Closing it still needs bound reviewer and auditor runs (for example ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION, which is only allowed for Low non-mandatory findings), so the effect is a misrepresented finding presented to those reviewers, not a direct gate pass. Hence Low.

findings.title: checkClosure still skips the 'fix is in the verified round candidate' check when the verifying round's source_commit is absent, a predicate that forged round metadata alone can satisfy. A PRESENT fix committed after the verifier's run started (so absent from both the round candidate and the run's head) still closes the finding
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:733 runs `if (commitPresent(repo, round.source_commit) && !isAncestor(fix, round.source_commit))`. round.source_commit is orchestrator metadata that checkReviewRounds (:752) only requires to equal the round manifest's source_commit, and findManifest (:895-913) tolerates a manifest whose source_commit does not exist. SEC23-7 in docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-23/sec23-repro.tests.mjs.txt (run by run-sec23-repro.sh on a --no-local clone of 6438e20; log sec23-repro.log) sets up round 2 to verify F-DG0-101 (High, mandatory) and round 3 as the gate round on a new candidate. The fix commit is a content change committed AFTER round 2's runs started, so it is not an ancestor of the round-2 verifier's head_commit_at_start (fix-in-verifier-head=false). Control, round 2 genuine (source_commit present): 1 error, 'fix … is not in the verified round-2 candidate'. Forged, round 2's committed manifest and stages entry name source_commit 'deadbeef'x5, entries self-consistent: 0 errors. D-039 closed the ABSENT-fix variant (SEC23-2/3: all-zero and typo'd fixes are rejected), and the fix must still be an ancestor of the gate candidate (SEC23-4). What remains is only the round-level binding: the reviewer's PASS is recorded as verifying a fix its run could not have seen. Real-repo census (tolerance-census.log): the only absent round is 18, and no CLOSED_VERIFIED closure is verified in round 18. So the skipped branch has no legitimate use today and is reachable only through forged round metadata. Exploitation still needs a genuine reviewer PASS verification in the forged round, so the effect is a mis-attributed fix_revision, not an unfixed finding in the gate candidate.
findings.expected: A CLOSED_VERIFIED closure must be tied to content the verifying run could actually see, whatever the round metadata says. Two options: (a) additionally require isAncestor(fix_revision, meta.head_commit_at_start) of the verifying run (always present and 40-hex after D-039, and a descendant of the round's source_commit in every legitimate case); or (b) reject a CLOSED_VERIFIED closure verified in a round whose source_commit is absent (no current closure depends on one). Optionally also require head_commit_at_start to be reachable from HEAD (isAncestor(head, HEAD)), not merely present in the object store, so an unreachable local object cannot change a verdict between clone modes (fail-closed in CI today). Add a fixture test like SEC23-7.

findings.title: D-040 replaced the round-candidate ancestry check instead of adding to it. In a GENUINE round (no forged metadata), a candidate-scope fix committed after the round froze but before the verifier's run started now closes a finding even though it is not in the frozen candidate the verifier reviewed. Round 23's validator rejected this
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:737-739 (at 6db3b83) now checks only isAncestor(fix_revision, verifyingRun.head_commit_at_start). The earlier `commitPresent(round.source_commit) && !isAncestor(fix, round.source_commit)` check was removed, not kept alongside. checkInvocation (:388-405) requires the head to be present, 40-hex and to contain the round manifest. Nothing requires the head's candidate CONTENT to equal the round candidate, i.e. that only metadata was committed between the freeze and the run start. SEC24-6 in docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-24/sec24-repro.tests.mjs.txt (run by run-sec24-repro.sh on --no-local clones; log sec24-repro.log) uses the stock fixture. Round 2 is genuine (its source_commit is present). A content change to src/app.txt is committed after the round-2 freeze, the round-2 runs start from that commit, the round-2 code-security run verifies F-DG0-101 (High, mandatory) with fix_revision = that commit, and round 3 is the gate round on a candidate containing it. Probe output: 'fix in round-2 frozen candidate: false; verifier head content hashes to round-2 candidate: false'. At 6438e20 (round-23 baseline): 1 error, 'fix … is not in the verified round-2 candidate'. At 6db3b83 (this candidate): 0 errors.
findings.expected: A CLOSED_VERIFIED closure stays bound to the frozen candidate the verifying round reviewed, as well as to the run head. Either (a) keep the D-040 run-head check AND restore `if (commitPresent(round.source_commit) && !isAncestor(fix, round.source_commit)) error`, or preferably (b) in checkInvocation, when binding.manifestPath is given, require candidateId(manifestFromRef(head, manifest.spec)) to equal the round's candidate_id. That means only metadata-only commits between the freeze and the run start. It binds the run head's content to the reviewed candidate and makes the run-head ancestry check equivalent to 'in the reviewed candidate'. The real-repo census (closure-census.log, --no-local clone) shows all 61 computable review-run heads already hash to their round candidate. The 2 non-computable runs are round 18's D-034-orphaned heads, and neither is a verifying or gate run. Option (b) therefore breaks no genuine record. Also correct the checkClosure error text 'it was not in the candidate the reviewer saw' (:739), which the head check does not establish without (b). Add a fixture test like SEC24-6.

So this is a mis-attribution, not an unreviewed fix in the gate. Real-repo census: 0 of 110 closures depend on it.

findings.title: D-044 claims every commit-id field the gate depends on must be a commit object, but a review round's source_commit (stages.json review_rounds[].source_commit and the round manifest) still accepts an annotated-tag object id
findings.reproduction: Candidate 331407e (sha256:1af91e8f...). D-044 (docs/delivery/decisions.md:39) says the change closes 'the whole "tag object id where a commit is required" class in one pass' and lists 'every commit-id field the gate depends on'. The gate source_commit (rules.mjs:966, D-037), fix_revision (rules.mjs:744) and head_commit_at_start (rules.mjs:399) are type-checked. A review round's source_commit is not: findManifest recomputes the round manifest with manifestFromRef(repo, m.source_commit, ...) (rules.mjs:918), which peels a tag to its tree; checkReviewRounds (rules.mjs:774-775) only compares the manifest's source_commit with stages.json; and checkClosure's anchor 1 uses commitPresent(round.source_commit) (cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}, which peels) and isAncestor (merge-base --is-ancestor, which peels) at rules.mjs:750-752. Probe SEC28-8 (test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-28/sec28b-roundsource.tests.mjs.txt, run in a disposable --no-local clone at 331407e): in the stock fixture, `git tag -a sec28round <frozen commit>` gives a tag object; a round manifest with source_commit set to that tag id makes findManifest return 0 errors, and `merge-base --is-ancestor <fix> <tag>` is true (peeled). Not reachable through the tooling: candidate.mjs --freeze writes `git rev-parse HEAD` (candidate.mjs:49/68/71), so only a hand-forged freeze could store a tag id. The gate ROUND can't hold one either, because its manifest source_commit must equal the commit-typed gate source_commit. The real repository is clean: all 27 resolvable round source_commits are commit objects; round 18 is the known D-034/D-035 absent one (objtype-census.log).
findings.expected: Consistent with D-044's stated scope: every commit-id field that a gate decision depends on, including review_rounds[].source_commit and the round manifest's source_commit, must be a commit object (objectType === 'commit'), with a tag rejected as for the gate source_commit. Otherwise D-044 should say that round source_commits are excluded, and why.
findings.actual: A tag-object round source_commit is accepted by findManifest, checkReviewRounds and checkClosure anchor 1: each peels it to the commit it names. This fails closed rather than open. The tag only aliases the same commit, so the content recompute and the ancestry anchors judge the correct commit. If the tag is deleted, a fresh clone lacks the tag object (SEC28-8: after tag -d + gc it's absent), and anchor 1 then rejects any closure verified in that round (F-DG0-169, SEC27-3). The residual is the same ref-dependent traceability-pointer inconsistency that F-DG0-250 fixed for fix_revision, plus the overstated completeness claim in D-044. It is not a gate bypass.

findings.title: P1 lets a transformation be closed (terminal, irreversible) by a plain status edit, with no G6 approval, no validated value and no reason

findings.expected: Playbook B0014 'Benefits before closure' and M0092 (delivery, adoption, validated value and transformation closure are separate statuses). The register specifies the control: REQ-S03-003 'close-transformation: TL after G6 approval' and 'the API rejects a closure request while validated value is pending'; REQ-PB-009 'closure requires validated benefits and sustainment owner'. findings.title: The sandboxed installer does not contain dependency code: the orchestrator's full environment (credentials) is passed in with host network, and the repository's control paths (.git/hooks, .claude, tools/gates, .github) are writable
findings.reproduction: tools/deps/install-sandbox.sh:76-96 builds the bwrap argv without --clearenv (and without --unshare-user/--cap-drop), and :82 binds the WHOLE repository writable. Probe (disposable clone, writable pnpm store in $TMPDIR): `FAKE_ORCH_SECRET=... tools/deps/install-sandbox.sh --root <clone> run -- bash -c 'env; grep CapEff /proc/self/status; echo > .git/hooks/pre-commit; echo > .claude/x; echo > tools/gates/x; echo > .github/workflows/x'`. Result: FAKE_ORCH_SECRET and the host's GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, CLOUDSDK_AUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN are all visible inside (names recorded only, values never printed); uid 0 with CapEff 000001ffffffffff; all four control paths are WRITABLE (a new tmpfs mount also succeeds; a remount of / rw was refused in this container). Failure scenario: an allow-listed lifecycle script, or any package code executed by `run` (D-046: build/typecheck/lint/test 'only inside the sandbox' -- vitest, eslint, vite plugins), reads the orchestrator's credentials and either sends them over the shared host network (an allow-listed host such as the GitHub API or the package registry suffices) or writes .git/hooks/pre-commit, which then executes UNSANDBOXED with the orchestrator's privileges at the next commit, or edits tools/gates/** or .claude/** to weaken the delivery controls. This defeats the stated purpose (D-046: 'a dependency's install script would otherwise run against the real filesystem and secrets').
findings.expected: REQ-DLV-042: the orchestrator never runs package code with its own privileges. Inside the sandbox: a cleared environment (only the variables pnpm/node need), only the dependency target trees (node_modules, build outputs) and the package store writable, with .git, .claude, tools/gates, tools/agents, tools/deps, .github and other control paths re-bound read-only (or a separate working copy), capabilities dropped (--unshare-user or --cap-drop ALL), and acceptance tests that prove each of these.
findings.actual: All host environment variables, including credentials, reach dependency code; .git/hooks, .claude, tools/gates and .github are writable from inside; the process keeps the full root capability set.

history.note: Raised in DG1 round 1 by code-security-reviewer; probe reproduced in a disposable clone.

findings.fix_summary: Installer redesigned (D-051): the real repo is bound --ro-bind and never writable inside the sandbox; create/frozen run pnpm in a disposable source copy and only node_modules (+ create lockfile) is copied back. Acceptance 12/12.

verification.note: The F-DG1-102-specific defects are fixed: the installer runs with --clearenv (only PATH/HOME/XDG/PNPM/registry/CI and the proxy/TLS variables cross; FAKE_ORCH_SECRET and every other host variable absent), CapEff 0000000000000000, real repo bound read-only (all direct control-path writes, remount and umount refused). AC-6 passes. The remaining control-path exposure is a different mechanism (copy-back from the disposable copy) and is tracked as F-DG1-118 (High, mandatory, OPEN) together with F-DG1-113/114.

findings.title: OIDC login CSRF: the `state` is not bound to the browser that started the login, so a callback URL obtained by one user signs another browser in as that user
findings.reproduction: apps/api/src/modules/identity/routes.ts:218-231 (GET /auth/login) stores state/nonce/verifier server-side (oidc.ts:52-76) but sets NO browser-binding cookie; routes.ts:238-276 (GET /auth/callback) accepts any request carrying a valid unexpired state (oidc.ts:79-86), revokes the presenting browser's current session (routes.ts:130) and starts a new one. Repro docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-1/repro-oidc-login-csrf.test.ts (fake IdP harness, real openid-client validation): attacker calls /auth/login, authenticates at the IdP as attacker-sub, and stops; the victim's browser (holding its own valid session) opens /auth/callback?code=..&state=.. -> 302, /auth/login Set-Cookie = null, victim's browser now signed in as `attacker-sub`, victim's original session -> 401. PKCE does not help because the verifier is looked up by state on the server.
findings.expected: RFC 6749 §10.12 / OIDC Core §3.1.2.1: the state (or a separate value) is bound to the initiating user-agent, e.g. an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, __Host- prefixed, short-lived login cookie whose hash is stored with oidc_login_state and required (and cleared) at the callback; a callback without the matching cookie is refused and audited, and the presenting browser's existing session is not revoked.
findings.actual: Any browser that presents a valid code+state completes the login as the IdP user who authenticated, and loses its own session.

history.note: Raised in DG1 round 1 by code-security-reviewer; reproduced with the fake-IdP harness.

findings.fix_summary: OIDC state bound to the initiating browser via a short-lived __Host-/HttpOnly/SameSite cookie (SHA-256 stored, migration 0007); a mismatched callback is refused+audited, state not consumed.

verification.note: OIDC login is browser-bound. Four cross-browser variants (callback in another browser, cookie swap, replay, forged cookie) all refused and audited; state not consumed.

findings.title: check-ci-needs.mjs can be bypassed: a job-level `if: always()` / `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` makes a product job run after delivery-gates FAILED, and the check still reports OK
findings.reproduction: deploy/scripts/check-ci-needs.mjs:33-52 only verifies that every job reaches delivery-gates through `needs:`. In GitHub Actions a job-level status-check function (always(), !cancelled(), failure()) overrides the implicit success() and runs the job even when a needed job failed. Disposable clone: add `if: always()` under `verify:` (or `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` under `images:`, which pushes images on protected branches) -> `node deploy/scripts/check-ci-needs.mjs` prints OK and exits 0 (check-ci-needs-negative.log N4, N5). The checker correctly rejects a removed `needs`, a rogue job and an unknown need (N1-N3). The current ci.yml is compliant.
findings.expected: The REQ-DLV-025 structural check fails any job (or the job chain to it) whose `if:` uses always(), !cancelled(), failure() or other status functions, or otherwise proves that each product job runs only when delivery-gates succeeded.
findings.actual: Status-function conditions pass the check unnoticed, so a later CI edit could silently re-enable product jobs after a failed gate.

history.note: Raised in DG1 round 1 by code-security-reviewer; bypass reproduced in a disposable clone.

findings.fix_summary: Closed with F-DG1-120: the gate checkout step's with: inputs are now allow-listed, so no ref/repository override can weaken the gate.

findings.title: NODE_ENV=production accepts an http APP_BASE_URL, which silently drops the Secure flag and the __Host- prefix from the session cookie
findings.reproduction: packages/config/src/load.ts:129-145 accepts http: or https: for APP_BASE_URL regardless of NODE_ENV; apps/api/src/modules/identity/sessions.ts:277-279 and routes.ts:63-64 derive the cookie name and `secure` from that protocol. deploy/compose/compose.yaml:76-78 runs the api with NODE_ENV=production and a default APP_BASE_URL of http://localhost:3000. A production deployment with a mistyped http:// origin behind a TLS-terminating proxy would therefore issue a non-Secure, non-__Host- session cookie, contrary to ADR-0005 §3 ('HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/, with the __Host- prefix in HTTPS deployments').
findings.expected: With NODE_ENV=production, APP_BASE_URL must be https (as OIDC_ISSUER_URL already is, load.ts:192-194), except for an explicit loopback host (localhost/127.0.0.1) used by the local Compose stack.
findings.actual: Any http origin is accepted in production.

history.note: Raised in DG1 round 1 by code-security-reviewer (source review).

findings.fix_summary: Production refuses an http APP_BASE_URL (except localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1]) at startup and in session setup, so the Secure flag / __Host- prefix cannot be silently dropped.

verification.note: The assembled production API with NODE_ENV=production refuses http://mth.example.com, http://10.0.0.5:3000 and http://localhost.example.com at startup (exit 78, 'APP_BASE_URL must use https when NODE_ENV=production ... loopback host'); https and loopback http start; development http is accepted.

findings.title: install-sandbox.sh control-path read-only protection is circumventable: the writable parent directories of the protected paths let dependency code replace a protected subtree, and config surfaces that do not yet exist are unprotected
findings.reproduction: In a disposable clone, the reviewer ran the committed probe (see evidence). Direct writes to the protected paths (.git, .claude, .github, tools/{gates,agents,deps}, docs/delivery, CLAUDE.md) are correctly refused. The gap: the installer binds the whole repo tree writable and re-binds only specific existing children read-only, so (1) a protected subtree can be moved aside and recreated because its PARENT directory is writable, and (2) protected config files that are absent from the tree are never bound, so they can be created. Full host-side demonstration in the evidence log.
findings.expected: Code running under the installer sandbox can write only node_modules and, in create mode, the lockfile; every other repo path, including the installer and the delivery/agent tooling, is immutable, and no new control/config file can be planted.
findings.actual: The installer itself, the gate/agent tooling and the delivery records can be altered on the host, and Claude/MCP/IDE config files can be planted, because the repo is writable and protection is applied only to specific existing children.

history.note: Reported by code-security-reviewer in DG1 round 2. Transcribed by the orchestrator from the reviewer's result and committed evidence; the agent's own write was blocked by a safety classifier. Full reproduction is in the cited evidence log.

verification.note: Run mode: AC-5/AC-7 PASS (parent rename, installer append, delivery-record write refused; repo unchanged). create/frozen: the copy-back mechanism (F-DG1-118) no longer lets dependency code write any control path (.git, tools/gates, docs/delivery, .claude) in the real tree; verified with the round-3 and extended round-4 repros.

findings.title: The derived creator assignment (F-DG1-106) can outlive a concurrent revocation of its source BU grant (write-skew), so a Transformation Lead keeps record access after the grant is revoked
findings.reproduction: An integration reproduction (3/3, see evidence) interleaves a create and a revoke of the source BU grant under READ COMMITTED: the create reads the source as active and inserts the derived transformation-scope row while the revoke's cascade cannot yet see that row; both commit, leaving an active derived assignment whose source is revoked. The Lead's live session is ended by the revoke, but after signing in again the Lead can read the record.

findings.title: The integration project is non-deterministic on the frozen candidate: 2 of 3 full runs exited 1 (one unhandled 57P01 from the new F-DG1-115 race suite, one a12 'denied create wrote a row' false red), because vitest ignores the project-level fileParallelism:false
findings.reproduction: Disposable clone of commit 5204179 (candidate f0baa87d0163560f), node_modules copied from the repository, PostgreSQL 16.13 throwaway cluster per run. bash docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/domain/round-3/03-integration-run.sh, three times. Run 1: 197/197 passed but vitest exit 1 on an Uncaught Exception 'terminating connection due to administrator command' (FATAL 57P01, database mth_f115_*), attributed to apps/api/test/integration/access-derived-race.test.ts: its afterAll drops the scratch database WITH (FORCE) (packages/db/test/global-setup.ts dropScratchDatabase) while a pooled client without an error listener is still connected. Run 2: 196/197, tests/qa/integration/a12-cross-scope.test.ts 'create is denied outside the caller's scope' failed with 'a denied create wrote a row: expected 33 to be 30'. Run 3: 197/197, exit 0. The a12 file alone, five times on fresh clusters: 14/14 each (06-a12-isolated.out.txt). Root cause of run 2: vitest.config.ts sets fileParallelism:false inside the integration project's test block, but vitest 3.2.4 lists fileParallelism in NonProjectOptions (node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/reporters.d.*.d.ts: type ProjectConfig = Omit<InlineConfig, NonProjectOptions | ...>), so files still run concurrently (run 2: summed test time 24.4 s > wall time 17.0 s); a12 counts every transformation row in the shared per-run database (startApi() without a scratch database), so creates by a concurrently running file are counted as if the denied creates had written them.
findings.expected: A required DG1 check (the integration project behind REQ-S19-004, REQ-S19-006 and REQ-DLV-033) gives the same verdict on the same candidate: either files really run serially (fileParallelism at the root config, or a per-project pool option that vitest honours), or suites that count rows on the shared database count only their own rows (or use a scratch database); and scratch databases are dropped only after every pool client has ended, or clients carry an error listener so a forced drop cannot surface as an uncaught exception.
findings.actual: The product behaviour is correct in every run: the five denied creates each returned 403/404 problem+json (asserted before the count), a refused create runs inside one transaction that rolls back (apps/api/src/modules/transformations/routes.ts: authorization precedes the insert), the a12 file is green in isolation 5/5, and migrations (8/8, migrate+catalogue 16/16), closure refusal (3/3), F-DG1-115 race (4/4) and contract (9/9) pass in all three runs. But a red integration run on an unchanged candidate cannot be told apart from a real access-control regression without manual triage like this, and the a12 assertion that guards 'a denied create writes nothing' is the one that flakes.

findings.title: install-sandbox.sh copy-back escape: every directory NAMED node_modules anywhere in the disposable workspace is copied into the real repo at the same path, so sandboxed dependency code can plant files under .claude/, .git/, tools/gates/, docs/delivery/ and create new config directories; a newline in a directory name also makes the installer rm -rf / mkdir outside the repo root
findings.reproduction: tools/deps/install-sandbox.sh:142-148 (D-051): `while IFS= read -r nm; do rel="${nm#"$WS"/}"; dest="$REPO_ROOT/$rel"; mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"; rm -rf "$dest"; cp -a "$nm" "$dest"; done < <(find "$WS" -type d -name node_modules -prune)`. The disposable copy $WS is fully writable by package code during create/frozen (line 124), and the loop trusts its layout. Reproduction (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-3/repro-copyback-escape.sh, log 13-copyback-escape.log): a scratch git project with .claude/, tools/gates/, docs/delivery/ and ONE allow-listed local dependency (pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies = ["evil"], exactly the case the sandbox exists to contain) whose postinstall writes, inside $WS, .claude/rules/node_modules/injected.md, .claude/skills/node_modules/SKILL.md, .claude/commands/node_modules/pwn.md, .claude/agents/node_modules/evil.md, .git/hooks/node_modules/x, tools/gates/node_modules/x, docs/delivery/node_modules/x, .vscode/node_modules/x and a directory named 'h\n..' containing victim/node_modules. Control: a direct write to the real root from inside the sandbox is refused (Read-only file system). Result of `install-sandbox.sh --root <scratch> create`: exit 0; on the HOST, after the installer exited, all 8 planted files are PRESENT in the real root; `git status --porcelain` shows only the new pnpm-lock.yaml (the planted paths are git-ignored by `node_modules/`, so AC-7's git-status check cannot see them); and the sibling directory <scratch>/../victim/node_modules (OUTSIDE --root) was DELETED: find printed the 'h\n..' path as two lines, the second ('../victim/node_modules') became rel, so the installer ran mkdir -p / rm -rf on $REPO_ROOT/../victim/node_modules; the following cp failed ('cannot stat'), but the loop ignores cp failures and the installer still exits 0. Secondary: tools/deps/tests/install-sandbox.test.sh:124-125,139 cleans up with `rm -rf "$ROOT/CLAUDE.local.md" "$ROOT/.mcp.json" "$ROOT/.vscode" ...` and `mv` on the REAL repo, so running the acceptance test deletes a developer's own pre-existing .vscode/ or CLAUDE.local.md. Precondition today: pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies is [] in the root package.json, so no third-party lifecycle script runs in the real repo now; the defect is in the control that is meant to contain such a script as soon as one is allow-listed (and any workspace package's own install script runs in $WS too).
findings.expected: REQ-DLV-042 / D-051: dependency code running under the installer can change ONLY the dependency target trees (the node_modules of the workspace's actual packages) and, in create, pnpm-lock.yaml; no file can appear under .claude/, .git/, tools/, docs/delivery/, .github/ or any other control/config path, and nothing outside the repo root is touched. Suggested direction: copy back only the node_modules of the known workspace package directories (root + the pnpm-workspace.yaml package globs resolved on the HOST from the real tree), read paths NUL-delimited (find -print0 / read -d ''), refuse any rel path containing '..' or a newline or resolving outside REPO_ROOT, fail (non-zero) on any copy error, and add acceptance cases that run the planted lifecycle script through create/frozen (not only `run`) and assert no file outside the expected node_modules set changed (including git-ignored ones). The acceptance test must not rm -rf/mv pre-existing paths of the real repo.
findings.actual: Dependency code can create arbitrary files under every protected path of the real repository (including Claude Code rules/skills/commands/agents directories that later agent and orchestrator sessions load, and inside .git/), invisibly to git status, and can make the orchestrator delete directories outside the repo root; the installer reports success (exit 0).

history.note: Raised by code-security-reviewer in DG1 round 3 (new mechanism of the F-DG1-113/F-DG1-114 root cause after the D-051 redesign); reproduced in a scratch project under $TMPDIR with the candidate's installer.

After in-app (client-side) navigation to the list and back, still 0 and 0. After page.reload(), 1 and 1. TransformationCreatePage.tsx:119 invalidates only ['transformations'], not keys.me, so the derived transformation-scope grant that the server adds on create (F-DG1-106) is absent from the client's grants, and `canOn(me, ...)` is false for the new record. findings.title: install-sandbox.sh copy-back hardening: copy errors are ignored (installer exits 0 after a failed/partial cp), and the destination set is 'any package.json at depth <= 4 on disk' rather than the pnpm-workspace.yaml members its comment claims
findings.reproduction: Static, tools/deps/install-sandbox.sh @016433d. (a) Lines 150-151 `rm -rf "$dest"; cp -a "$wsnm" "$dest"` have no error check and line 155 is an unconditional `exit 0`: if cp fails (ENOSPC from a dependency that fills the disposable copy, I/O error), the real member's node_modules has already been deleted or is partial and the installer still reports success. F-DG1-118's expected outcome asked to 'fail (non-zero) on any copy error'. A dynamic attempt (an unreadable directory planted in node_modules) was stopped earlier by pnpm itself (EACCES, exit 243), so this part is not reproduced dynamically. (b) Line 153 enumerates `find "$REPO_ROOT" -maxdepth 4 -name package.json -not -path '*/node_modules/*'` on the real FILESYSTEM (tracked and untracked), while the comment (lines 138-143) says 'the root and every committed package.json directory' and pnpm-workspace.yaml declares only apps/* and packages/*. Today the two sets are identical (8 paths, verified), so there is no current exploit; but any future package.json at depth <= 4 outside the workspace (e.g. a test fixture such as tools/gates/fixtures/package.json, or an untracked one) silently becomes a copy-back destination where dependency code can plant a node_modules that scripts in that directory would resolve.
findings.expected: Fail non-zero on any rm/cp error in the copy-back; derive the destinations from pnpm-workspace.yaml globs (plus the root) resolved on the real tree, or from `git ls-files` package.json entries, matching the documented contract.

findings.title: Module lint rule 3 (native loaders process.binding/_linkedBinding/dlopen) is bypassed by aliasing process through an import of node:process
findings.reproduction: Candidate 24eb3779 (commit 5f83a336), disposable clone. apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts:290 flags `<root>.binding|_linkedBinding|dlopen` only when rootName() (line 131-134) sees the identifier text `process`/`globalThis`/`global`; BANNED_PRIMITIVES (57-72) does not contain binding/_linkedBinding/dlopen; and node:process is not in LOADER_BUILTINS (51-55), so bareAllowed() accepts it as a `node:` built-in. Plants through fileViolations('transformations', .../planted.ts): `import proc from "node:process"; proc.dlopen({exports:{}} as any, "/tmp/x.node")` -> 0 violations; `(proc as any).binding("fs")` -> 0; `import { dlopen } from "node:process"` -> 0 (22-plant-f124.log X6-X8). Written as a real file apps/api/src/modules/access/zz-planted.ts (`import { binding } from "node:process"; ... binding("fs")`, or the dlopen form), the candidate's architecture.test.ts stays green, 74/74, exit 0 (22b-plant-f124-module-tree.log). Runtime, Node 22.22.2: the default export of node:process is `process` itself, and the named exports binding and dlopen are functions; binding('fs') returns the internal fs binding, binding('natives') exposes the built-in JS sources, and dlopen attempts a native load (ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED for a missing file) (23-node-process-alias-runtime.log). The same forms written with the identifier `process` ARE caught (X9; the candidate's own P12 case).
findings.expected: The testkit header claims rule 3 bans the native loaders process.binding / process._linkedBinding / process.dlopen, and that rules 1-2 'remove every syntactic route inside module source'. To make that hold: add binding/_linkedBinding/dlopen to the banned names (rule 1, every syntactic form), or treat an import of node:process (default, namespace or named) as an alias of the runtime root, or ban the node:process specifier in src/modules (process is a global, so a module never needs the import). Then add the X6-X8 forms to the self-check table.
findings.actual: The three native-loader primitives are reachable from module source through an import of node:process without any violation. Impact is limited. Neither primitive is a JS module loader that hands out another module's internals. dlopen needs a compiled .node file on disk; binding gives raw internal bindings (fs, natives). This is a static architecture lint (defence in depth, ADR-0002), not a runtime security boundary, and the required plants of F-DG1-124 (constructed key, Reflect.get) are all caught. Hence Low, not mandatory.

findings.title: install-sandbox.sh copy-back member resolver reads every YAML list item in pnpm-workspace.yaml as a glob and ignores '!' exclusions, so non-member directories can become copy-back destinations
findings.reproduction: tools/deps/install-sandbox.sh:154-168 (candidate 5f83a336). The node resolver matches /^\s*-\s*["']?([^"'\n#]+?)["']?\s*$/gm over the WHOLE file, not only the `packages:` sequence, and passes every item to fs.globSync. fs.globSync has no negation, so a `!pattern` item matches nothing and never removes a member. Repro (repro-f123-copyback.sh Case B, unchanged installer, --root on a disposable workspace, offline): pnpm-workspace.yaml = packages: [apps/*, packages/*, "!apps/legacy"] plus publicHoistPattern: ["tools/x"]; apps/legacy and tools/x each have a package.json; an allow-listed dependency's postinstall plants node_modules/PWNED in the disposable copy at tools/x and apps/legacy. The resolver parses the globs as ["apps/*","packages/*","!apps/legacy","tools/x"] and lists apps/legacy and tools/x as members. pnpm itself reports 'Scope: all 3 workspace projects' (apps/legacy excluded), yet after `create` the REAL target tree has tools/x/node_modules/PWNED and apps/legacy/node_modules/PWNED (18-f123-copyback.log).
findings.expected: The destinations are exactly the pnpm workspace members, as the installer's own comment states ('the root plus every directory that the packages: globs in pnpm-workspace.yaml resolve to'): parse only the `packages:` sequence and apply `!` exclusions (or ask pnpm for the member list, e.g. `pnpm ls -r --depth -1 --json` run on the trusted real tree outside the sandbox), and add a test case with an exclusion and an unrelated list key.
findings.actual: Not exploitable on the committed tree. Today's pnpm-workspace.yaml has only the `packages:` sequence with apps/* and packages/* (case A: the resolver yields exactly root, apps/*, packages/* with a package.json; the stray tools/x/package.json is NOT a destination). The latent mismatch is reached only if a maintainer later adds a negated workspace pattern, or a list-valued pnpm setting (onlyBuiltDependencies, publicHoistPattern, ...) whose item names an existing directory with a package.json. The YAML is part of the trusted real tree (dependency code cannot change it), so this is hardening, not a current escape. Low, not mandatory.

verification.note: Fix 3037ce2 is in the candidate. Code: the copy-back member list now comes from `pnpm -r ls --depth -1 --json` run in the real REPO_ROOT, parsed by a string- and escape-aware array scanner. A path outside REPO_ROOT is refused and fails the install, and an empty or failed resolve fails the install. Frozen suite in a disposable clone (12-install-sandbox-tests.log): 13 PASS, including AC-10. The 14th case, AC-1 (effect), is BLOCKED only by registry access (ECONNREFUSED, 13-ac1-effect-offline-equivalent.log part 1). Its offline equivalent passes: same fixture, lockfile pinned to the store integrity, wrapper unchanged, and it exercises the new pnpm-ls path for a single-package root. So the claimed 14/14 is consistent with everything I can reproduce. Negative control (14-f126-negative-control.log): with the pre-fix installer (3037ce2^), AC-10 FAILS ('legacy=yes, toolsx=yes'), so the test detects the defect. AC-10 asserts only the root as a positive destination. My own probe (15-f126-member-probe.log, dg1-r6-installer-members-probe.sh, 5/5 PASS) therefore covers the rest. A NON-ROOT member with its own dependency receives node_modules. A '!'-excluded package and a publicHoistPattern directory receive nothing, although a build script planted node_modules there. A member whose name contains ']' and '"' and a nested packages/deep/inner member both receive node_modules. A `packages:` pattern pointing outside the root (../outside/*) is listed by pnpm, but the wrapper refuses both out-of-root paths and exits 1, and the outside directory gets nothing. Observations, not findings: the parser `continue`s past an array it cannot JSON.parse, so a partial parse failure would skip a member rather than fail the install (fail-incomplete, not an escape). findings.title: The D-054 and module-lint testkit statement that the loader/exec enumeration is 'exhaustive for the PINNED Node version (22.x)' names the wrong pinned runtime. findings.reproduction: Candidate e27eaf5f (freeze commit 11bc4c4). apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts:48-50 says: 'For the PINNED Node version (22.x) the concrete loader/exec built-ins and process.* methods are now enumerated exhaustively, as validated by the round-7 code-security sweep'. D-054 in docs/delivery/decisions.md says 'EXHAUSTIVE for the pinned Node version' and 'enumerated exhaustively for the pinned Node 22'. The repository pins Node 24 as the runtime: .nvmrc = 24; deploy/docker/Dockerfile:24 ARG NODE_IMAGE=node:24-bookworm-slim@sha256:0e0ff40c…; ADR-0001 §1 says 'Target runtime: the Node.js 24 LTS line in every container image', with Node 22.18+ only the 'Supported floor'; and the deploy/ci/ci.yml verify matrix is ['24','22']. package.json engines is '>=22.18.0 <25'. Evidence: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/domain/round-8/11-node-pin.out.txt. The F-DG1-128 report itself calls Node 22.22.2 'the version the repo pins'.
findings.expected: The exhaustiveness statement names the version it was actually validated on (the Node 22.22.2 build sandbox, the supported floor). For the production target, Node 24, there are two options. (a) Sweep Node 24's builtinModules (including the prefix-only node: modules, which builtinModules omits) and its process.* members the same way, then state the claim for both. (b) Say explicitly that the Node 24 target is not yet swept and falls under residual (c) until it is. D-054's reopen criterion ('a later Node version adds …') should also cover the current target runtime, not only a future one.
findings.actual: The claim describes Node 22 as 'the pinned version', but production runs Node 24. Residual (c) is narrowed to 'genuinely FUTURE/UNKNOWN built-ins … of a LATER Node version'. Node 24 is already the shipped runtime, not a future one, so a Node-24-only loader route would fall outside both the claimed exhaustive set and the narrowed residual. I could not sweep Node 24 myself: this sandbox has only /opt/node20, /opt/node21 and /opt/node22, and no network. I therefore do not claim that such a route exists, only that the claim's validation scope is misstated. Impact is limited. This is a static defence-in-depth lint for ADR-0002 module boundaries over human-reviewed code, explicitly 'NOT a runtime security boundary'. No module uses any such route, and the CI matrix runs the lint on 24 as well, although the lint can only flag what it enumerates. Hence Low and not mandatory. It is a documentation-honesty defect, not a product or runtime defect. An ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION with a wording fix in the next stage would be reasonable.

findings.title: Module lint: in the pinned Node 22, process.kill(process.pid,'SIGUSR1') or process._debugProcess(process.pid) starts the V8 inspector in-process, which is the capability of the banned node:inspector. Global fetch and WebSocket then send Runtime.evaluate, which runs arbitrary code. The lint reports 0 violations, so D-054's 'exhaustive for the pinned Node 22' claim does not hold.
findings.reproduction: Candidate e27eaf5f (freeze commit 11bc4c4), disposable clone, Node 22.22.2. In apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts, PROCESS_LOADERS (line 122) is binding/_linkedBinding/dlopen/execve, and rule 3 (line 336) flags only those members on the global process. `process.kill`, `process._kill` and `process._debugProcess` are ordinary `root.member` uses, so they are allowed. Plant through fileViolations('transformations', .../probe.ts) (01-lint-probes.log). N1: `process.kill(process.pid, "SIGUSR1"); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500)); const list = await (await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:9229/json/list")).json(); const ws = new WebSocket(list[0].webSocketDebuggerUrl); await new Promise((r) => ws.addEventListener("open", r)); ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id: 1, method: "Runtime.evaluate", params: { expression: '<any JS>' } }));` gives 0 violations. N2: `process._debugProcess(process.pid);` gives 0 violations. Runtime proof (02-n1-runtime.log, source n1-sigusr1-inspector-runtime.mjs.txt): the same N1 code prints 'Debugger listening on ws://127.0.0.1:9229/...'. The evaluated expression process.getBuiltinModule("child_process").execSync("id") returns 'uid=0(root) gid=0(root)', which is code evaluation plus exec in the running process. N2 also opens the inspector. Production starts `node .../dist/main.js` without --disable-sigusr1 (deploy/docker/entrypoint.sh:30-31), so the route exists in the shipped runtime as well. No module uses process.kill/_kill/_debugProcess today (grep of apps/ and packages/ is empty).
findings.expected: D-054 and the testkit header (lines 48-57) say the concrete loader/exec built-ins and `process.*` methods are enumerated exhaustively for the pinned Node 22.x. Residual (c) is narrowed to future/unknown built-ins and WebAssembly/node:wasi. The header bans node:inspector as a loader built-in (line 89), so reaching the same inspector without the import is a loader/eval route that the enumeration should cover. It is neither future/unknown nor wasm. Suggested fix (any one, the first two together are best): (1) add `kill`, `_kill`, `_debugProcess` and `_debugEnd` to PROCESS_LOADERS (no module needs to signal processes), with self-checks N1/N2; (2) run the shipped node processes with `--disable-sigusr1` (present on the >=22.18 floor; 03-n1-remedy-probe.log shows the inspector then never listens: fetch ECONNREFUSED, and the process survives the signal); or (3) drop the 'exhaustive' wording and name this route as an accepted residual in the header and D-054.
findings.actual: Both plants pass the lint with zero violations, and the header and D-054 claim an exhaustive enumeration that this route contradicts. Impact is limited, as with F-DG1-125/127/128. The route needs a loopback network and visibly starts a debugger ('Debugger listening' on stderr). No module uses it today. Hence Low, not mandatory, and not blocking. It does not reopen F-DG1-128. findings.title: Module lint: the global process._debugProcess(process.pid) (or process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGUSR1')) activates the in-process inspector without importing node:inspector, and the Node globals fetch + WebSocket then evaluate an arbitrary code string via Runtime.evaluate. All of this passes with 0 violations, which contradicts the D-054 / testkit-header claim that the Node 22 loader/exec process.* methods are enumerated exhaustively.
findings.reproduction: Candidate sha256:e27eaf5f...44876 (freeze commit 11bc4c4, HEAD 6cb3813), disposable clone, Node v22.22.2. (1) Sweep (14-adjacent-sweep.log): the process function members on this Node include _debugProcess, _debugEnd and kill, and none of them is in PROCESS_LOADERS (binding, _linkedBinding, dlopen, execve). (2) Runtime (15-adjacent-debugprocess-runtime.log, script docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/qa/tests/dg1-r8-debugprocess-runtime-probe.mjs): process._debugProcess(process.pid) prints 'Debugger listening on ws://127.0.0.1:9229/...'. Then fetch('http://127.0.0.1:9229/json/list') and new WebSocket(webSocketDebuggerUrl) send Runtime.evaluate with the string 'globalThis.__qa = 6*7; process.versions.node'. The reply is {"result":{"type":"string","value":"22.22.2"}}, globalThis.__qa reads 42 in the same process, and the exit code is 0. No module is imported. (3) Lint (16-adjacent-debugprocess-lint.log, probe docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/qa/tests/dg1-r8-debugprocess-lint-probe.test.ts) through the candidate's own fileViolations('transformations', .../zz-qa-planted.ts): D1, the full route as module source (_debugProcess + fetch + WebSocket + Runtime.evaluate of a parameter string), gives violations = []. D2 `process._debugProcess(process.pid);` gives []. D3 `process.kill(process.pid, "SIGUSR1");` gives []. No repository launch script, Dockerfile or NODE_OPTIONS sets --disable-sigusr1, which this Node supports.
findings.expected: The testkit header residual (c) and D-054 say that for the pinned Node 22 'the concrete loader/exec built-ins and process.* methods are now enumerated exhaustively', and that residual (c) is narrowed to future/unknown built-ins/methods of a later Node and WebAssembly/node:wasi. The inspector is already a banned loader built-in (`inspector`/`node:inspector`), and rule 1 bans code evaluation (eval/Function). So a module should not be able to reach inspector-based code evaluation through an existing Node 22 process.* method with 0 violations. Either close the route, for example by adding `_debugProcess` (and `_debugEnd`) to PROCESS_LOADERS, plus a rule-3 check or a runtime `--disable-sigusr1` for the `process.kill(<self>, 'SIGUSR1')` spelling, with self-checks. Or name it as a stated and accepted residual and remove the word 'exhaustively' from the header and D-054. The default-deny `node:`/process allow-list that the header already mentions would also close this class.
findings.actual: All three plants report 0 violations, and the route works at runtime on the pinned Node. It is not covered by any stated residual: (a) is third-party data flow, (b) is code generation followed by a literal own-module import, and (c) as amended by D-054 covers only future/unknown built-ins or methods and WebAssembly/wasi, while _debugProcess and kill exist in today's Node 22.22.2. Impact is limited, as with F-DG1-125/127/128. The lint is static defence-in-depth for the ADR-0002 module boundaries over human-reviewed code, explicitly not a runtime security boundary. No module uses _debugProcess, SIGUSR1, fetch to 127.0.0.1:9229 or WebSocket today. The route also opens a loopback debug port, which is visible. Hence Low, not mandatory and not blocking. It does not reopen F-DG1-128, whose two routes are verifiably closed.

findings.title: Module lint: the allow-listed built-in node:crypto still exposes a native-code loader. crypto.setEngine(<path>) dlopen()s an arbitrary shared object, and its ELF constructor runs before the call throws. findings.reproduction: Candidate sha256:05915c32…babd (freeze commit 273d21f, HEAD 07f1a54), disposable full clone, Node v22.22.2 (OpenSSL 3.5.5). (1) Static: in apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts:77 SAFE_NODE_BUILTINS includes 'crypto', and bareAllowed (129-130) allows `node:crypto`. `setEngine` is not in BANNED_PRIMITIVES (79-94), so neither rule 1 nor rule 3 sees it. Planted through fileViolations('transformations', <MODULES_DIR>/transformations/zz-planted.ts, src): `import { setEngine } from "node:crypto"; export const f = (p: string) => setEngine(p);` gives 0 violations, and the namespace form `import * as c from "node:crypto"; … c.setEngine(p)` also gives 0 (test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-9/01-lint-probes.log, 'MEMBER PASSES-LINT'). (2) End to end (02-setengine-e2e.log): a real module file src/modules/transformations/zz-engine.ts calling setEngine(path) gives moduleViolations('transformations') = [] (0). Called at runtime with a gcc-built shared object whose __attribute__((constructor)) prints a marker (source setengine-eng.c.txt), it prints 'NATIVE-CONSTRUCTOR-RAN', so native code ran in the API process. setEngine then throws ERR_CRYPTO_ENGINE_UNKNOWN, but only after the library was loaded. The standalone probe (setengine-probe.mjs.txt) shows the same. The .so can be produced by the also allow-listed node:fs, so no non-allow-listed import is needed. findings.expected: D-055 and the testkit header (architecture.testkit.ts:70-75) state that none of the allow-listed built-ins 'loads, evaluates or executes code, opens a debugger, or loads native objects', and D-055 says the switch 'closes the whole loader/exec class at once … and prevents further adjacent-route findings'. Those members still depend on the Node version: a later Node could add a loader member to crypto/fs/util.
findings.actual: `import { setEngine } from "node:crypto"; setEngine(path)` in module source passes the lint with 0 violations and loads and runs native code (Node 22.22.2). The header's 'none of them … loads native objects' sentence and D-055's 'whole class closed' claim are inaccurate. Residuals (a)-(c) do not cover it: it is not data flow, not a JS import of generated code, and not WebAssembly.

findings.reproduction: Candidate sha256:18fee161…8807 (freeze commit 265af7e, HEAD 241a377), disposable full clone, Node v22.22.2 / OpenSSL 3.5.5, gcc. (1) Static: architecture.testkit.ts:101 adds `setEngine` to BANNED_PRIMITIVES, and rule 1 (visit, ~:304-309) matches identifiers and string literals whose text equals a banned name. Rule 2 flags only element-access keys that are not static. Nothing flags an allow-listed module namespace (`import * as c from "node:crypto"`) being used as a VALUE, e.g. passed to Object.entries/Object.values. Rule 3's 'used as a value' check (:338-353) applies only to process/globalThis/global/module. At runtime, each selector is identical (===) to crypto.setEngine. End to end (12-real-plant-enumeration.log on Node 22; 16-… on Node 24): with a real file at apps/api/src/modules/transformations/zz-qa-r10-enum-engine.ts containing `import * as c from "node:crypto"; … new Map(Object.entries(c)).get("set".concat("Engine"))(p)`, the real module-tree check 'every import respects dependsOn, public surfaces and allowed packages' stays GREEN (exit 0). findings.expected: The F-DG1-130 fix summary says setEngine is caught 'in every form', and residual (a) says 'rules 1-2 remove every syntactic route inside module source'. Either the member is unreachable from module source, or this route is a stated residual. A name ban works for constructor/eval-style primitives because their holders (process, globalThis, non-enumerable constructor, non-allow-listed modules) cannot be enumerated by module source. setEngine, however, is an ENUMERABLE export of an allow-listed module, so enumeration recovers it without the name. Rule 2 endorses Map lookups because 'a Map returns only what was put in it', and here the namespace's own entries are what is put in. Possible closures, for the implementer to choose: treat namespace/default bindings of allow-listed built-ins like runtime roots (only `ns.member` with a static, non-banned member; no value use such as passing to Object.values/entries/assign, spread or for-in); require named imports for node:crypto; or name 'enumeration of an allow-listed namespace' as a stated residual and correct the 'every form' and 'every syntactic route' wording. findings.title: Module lint test classification is wider than the build exclusion and the vitest include. apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts:177 sets TEST_FILE = /\.test\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/, and :461 isTest = TEST_FILE.test(file) grants the test allowances: :471 import of the composition-root files modules.ts / architecture.testkit.ts, and :480 import of vitest. But apps/api/tsconfig.build.json:10 excludes only src/**/*.test.ts, *.test.tsx and *.testkit.ts, and vitest.config.ts:21 collects only apps/api/src/**/*.test.ts. So a module file named *.test.mts / .test.cts (also .test.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx) is never run as a test, is compiled into dist, yet gets test-only exemptions from the boundary check. This is introduced by the F-DG1-134 fix (e71f3d0), and architecture.test.ts:763 pins the behaviour as intended. It is not a regression: before the fix such files were not scanned at all.
findings.reproduction: Candidate sha256:00f1498c...c80b, full disposable clone at 08cbd12, Node v22.22.2, after pnpm -r build. I planted apps/api/src/modules/kpi/zzgap.test.mts containing `import { API_MODULES } from "../../modules.ts"; export const moduleCount: number = Object.keys(API_MODULES).length;`. Results: (1) moduleViolations("kpi") = 0. (2) cd apps/api && pnpm build exits 0, and dist/modules/kpi/ contains zzgap.test.mjs (+ .d.mts). (3) node: import("./dist/modules/kpi/zzgap.test.mjs") gives moduleCount = 13, so it runs from the production artefact. (4) `vitest list --project unit-node` lists it 0 times, so it is not a test. (5) Control: the same content as zzgap.mts gives `modules/kpi/zzgap.mts: imports ../../modules.ts outside src/modules (composition root)`. The same exemption also admits `import ... from "vitest"` (a devDependency). Rules 1-5 (banned names, computed keys, runtime roots, syntax, node:crypto named-only) still apply to such files: the exemption is only the 2 composition-root files + vitest. Logs: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-13/03-test-name-allowance-gap.log and 01-F-DG1-134-reproof-probe.log (GAP probe case).
findings.expected: A module file gets test allowances only if it is really a test: excluded from the build AND collected by vitest. Either narrow TEST_FILE to the extensions the build excludes and vitest runs (today .test.ts; .test.tsx is excluded from the build and so also harmless), or widen tsconfig.build.json `exclude` (and, if wanted, the vitest include) to src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}. architecture.test.ts:763 should assert the chosen invariant, for example that a *.test.mts which the build would emit gets no exemption.
findings.actual: A production-shipped module file named *.test.mts (or .test.cts/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx) may import apps/api/src/modules.ts, apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts (which tsc then pulls into the build, dragging in the typescript devDependency) and vitest with 0 lint violations, though it is never run as a test.

history.note: Raised by code-security-reviewer in DG1 round 13 while verifying the F-DG1-134 fix.
